paragraphs: Bus and train fares in Ireland will go up by 15% in January. Now the transport authority says it will check fares every year.
In 2022, the Government cut fares by 20%. It wanted to help people with high living costs.
Official papers show that the finance department wanted the cut to end. It said the transport minister, Darragh O'Brien, agreed to this.
Anne Shaw is the head of the National Transport Authority. In a letter, she said fares have not gone up since 2018. But costs are higher now. Many fares are still cheap compared with other prices.
The minister says about 140 new or better services will start next year.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭的公車和火車票價將在一月上漲 15%。
現在交通主管機關表示，以後每年都會檢討票價。
2022 年，政府把票價調降了 20%。
政府想幫助生活成本高的人。
官方文件顯示，財政部門希望結束這項降價。
文件指出，交通部長達拉・歐布萊恩同意了這件事。
安妮・蕭是國家交通局的首長。
她在一封信中說，票價從 2018 年以來就沒有漲過。
但現在成本變高了。
和其他物價相比，許多票價仍然很便宜。
部長表示，明年將有大約 140 項新增或改善的服務上路。

paragraphs: Bus and train fares will go up by 15 per cent from January, and passengers may face more rises in the future. The National Transport Authority (NTA) plans to review fares every year.

In 2022, the Government cut bus and train fares by 20 per cent to help people with the rising cost of living. Official papers now show that the Department of Public Expenditure pushed hard for this cut to end. It said the Minister for Transport, Darragh O'Brien, had agreed to reverse it by the middle of 2026, as part of a €940 million funding deal.
In April, the department said it was unhappy that the change was late. It believed fare money should help pay for new services.

In a letter in August, NTA chief executive Anne Shaw told the minister that public transport fares had not risen since 2018, even though running costs had grown. She said many fares would still be lower than if they had followed inflation.
The minister says about 140 new and improved services will start next year.
sentZh: 公車和火車票價將從一月起上漲 15%，乘客未來可能還會面臨更多漲價。
國家交通局（NTA）計畫每年檢討票價。
2022 年，政府把公車和火車票價調降 20%，以幫助民眾應付不斷上升的生活成本。
官方文件現在顯示，公共支出部曾極力推動結束這項降價。
該部表示，交通部長達拉・歐布萊恩已同意在 2026 年年中前取消降價，作為一項 9.4 億歐元資金協議的一部分。
四月時，該部表示對這項變更延遲感到不滿。
該部認為，票價收入應該用來支付新服務。
國家交通局執行長安妮・蕭在八月的一封信中告訴部長，雖然營運成本增加，但大眾運輸票價自 2018 年以來都沒有上漲。

paragraphs: Bus and rail fares will be reviewed every year from now on, meaning passengers are likely to face further increases after a 15 per cent rise takes effect in January.

Official documents released by the Department of Transport show that the increase followed strong pressure from the Department of Public Expenditure. A 20 per cent fare cut had been introduced in 2022 as part of a cost-of-living package, and the department said Transport Minister Darragh O'Brien had agreed to reverse it by mid-2026 in return for a €940 million subsidy for public transport services.
In April, officials said they were "concerned and disappointed" that the reversal was behind schedule, arguing that fare revenue should help fund new services.

In a letter to the minister in August, National Transport Authority chief executive Anne Shaw said annual reviews would make subsidised routes more sustainable and give greater certainty over funding. She noted that fares had not increased since 2018 despite rising operating costs, and that many would remain below inflation-adjusted levels.
The minister insists that around 140 new and enhanced services will be introduced next year.

國家交通局執行長安妮・蕭在八月寫給部長的信中表示，每年檢討票價將使受補助的路線更能永續經營，也讓經費更有保障。
她指出，儘管營運成本上升，票價自 2018 年以來都沒有調漲，而且許多票價仍會低於經通膨調整後的水準。
部長堅稱，明年將推出約 140 項新增及強化的服務。

paragraphs: Commuters face the prospect of fare rises becoming a fixture, after it emerged that bus and rail fares will henceforth be reviewed annually. The disclosure comes ahead of a 15 per cent increase that takes effect in January.

Documents released by the Department of Transport reveal that the rise followed sustained pressure from the Department of Public Expenditure. The latter maintained that Transport Minister Darragh O'Brien had undertaken to unwind a 20 per cent fare cut, introduced in 2022 to cushion households against soaring living costs, by mid-2026, in exchange for a €940 million subsidy.
Officials voiced their dismay in April that the reversal had slipped behind schedule, contending that fare income ought to bankroll new services.

In correspondence with the minister, National Transport Authority chief executive Anne Shaw defended annual reviews as a means of placing subsidised routes on a sounder footing. She pointed out that fares had been frozen since 2018 notwithstanding escalating operating costs, and that many would still lag behind inflation.
The minister, for his part, maintains that some 140 new and upgraded services will be rolled out next year.
